title: The State of our Newsletter is Strong
subtitle: Transparency in absurdist newsletter publishing
text:
This is written as a playful State of the Union feature for transparency in newsletter writing. I hope you enjoy it!

I write some silly things. Apparently, writing “some silly thing,” and with occasional spelling mistakes, is hot. At least when it comes to engagement.

I have previously documented some of my work around understanding, with my human brain, what the heck is going on with my LinkedIn engagement (high). It continues to be good compared to a Imagined Less Weird content:

30,000% year over year growth in impressions!

Which also has translated into Followers:

And engagement:

The rate has been robust, but like all things it depends on how you slice it.

I am a fan of radical transparency, and will continue the trend with this very state of the newsletter report!

I am proud to announce, the state of our newsletter is strong. We have reached many readers in the past year:

This has, much to my surprise, also translated into a similar revenue curve, with more revenue per year than subscribers per year, which I am told, is abnormal:

It becomes a harder argument to write less often, less personally, and less absurdly when the numbers look like that.

On your subscriptions, of which I look forward to many more, it seems that my strategy of publishing free new content, and then locking some older content in the paywall section is a reliable strategy, compared to nothing. I don't get to see how other peoples newsletters are doing. That's a point of me doing this transparency report about my newsletter so that other people have something to look at and maybe even do a similar thing —because “comps.”

Generally, as a metric-enthusiast human, I am learning two things:

• perfect is the enemy of growth

• writing every day is better than not daily

• If you have trouble with number two, return to point one.

• Sometimes, you have to write a hit.

You also have to hustle. It's the only thing that works. This is, with a graphic obscuring the identities of individuals who have shared my articles, the list of how many times I have shared it, versus the data on the top people who fit on the screen, absent their identity:

Nobody is going to share your newsletter more than you. And this is limiting. Getting on the gravy train of somebody else doing a big something or other for you is not something to count on. You just have to keep cranking out engaging material. But it doesn't always have to be engaging, just enough. If you're waiting for magic, you're waiting too long.

I will learn a little bit more, and do a deeper dive, but if you're wondering whether the newsletter, as it stands, is doing a good enough job as a newsletter, my guess is the answer is yes?

I would of course deeply appreciate if any of my readers choose to subscribe, and even more and if you can choose to share it with people who might appreciate the work! The fact that anybody bothers to read what I write? It matters more than you can know.

I will remind folks that I have a podcast as well, and I would encourage you to rate that on Apple podcast and Spotify because it's a big deal and drives discovery:
